Sourced from a live visual-coverage audit (2026-08-20) that found several already-shipped Grade 9 skills — mostly map/geography content in Social Studies, plus two Pre-Technical skills — have content that genuinely needs a real photographic/illustrative image rather than a code-drawn SVG (maps, wood-grain texture, and multi-object workshop scenes are the recurring reasons an SVG type would misrepresent the content). howToUse: 1. Copy one entry's `prompt` field verbatim into fal.ai (nano banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
2. Save the returned image, then tell Claude which `id` it corresponds to and where the file was saved.

3. Claude will inspect the image with vision to confirm every letter actually printed on the image matches an item in that entry's `expectedLabels`, note (and skip, not guess) any duplicated/ambiguous printed letters, run `npm run images:webp` (from web/) to convert the source PNG to WebP in place, add/reuse an entry in the shared cross-skill registry `web/src/lib/photoImages.ts` (never inline the image/part data directly in a skill file), wire a multi-Bloom's-tier set of question branches into the skill file(s) named in `targetSkillFile` per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, and verify (tsc + lint + a real request against the running dev server) before calling it done.

4. If any part is missing an arrow/letter, or a letter's arrow lands on the wrong structure, regenerate with a corrected prompt (add an explicit correction line naming the missing/misplaced part) rather than accepting a partial image — every part in `expectedLabels` must be identifiable.

5. An image is not tied to the one skill in `targetSkillFile` — once registered in photoImages.ts, reuse it from any other skill (same or different subject, same grade) that has a genuine curriculum reason to reference it, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's photo-diagram section.
_meta.styleGuideSummary: All prompts embed the same style block so every generated image reads as one consistent visual system across the whole app — do not vary the style between images.
_meta.criticalRule: Every prompt instructs nano banana NOT to print any part's name as text anywhere on the image — only a circled capital letter + thin leader line per part. This is deliberate and different from typical stock 'labeled diagram' images (which usually print full text labels): text labels would give the answer away before the question is even asked. If a returned image has any part's name printed as text, it must be regenerated.
_meta.displayConstraint: Confirmed in web/src/components/visuals/Visual.tsx's PhotoDiagram renderer: images display at max-height 420px, max-width 672px (Tailwind max-w-2xl), object-contain, width 100% of container. Source images at roughly 1024-1200px on the long edge are plenty — this is never a print asset. The `dimensions` field on each entry below states the generation aspect ratio/size that best fits that constraint.
_meta.mapCaution: Several entries below depict Africa/country outlines. Keep every outline map GENERIC and UNLABELLED (no country names, no modern political borders beyond what's explicitly requested) per the same pattern already used successfully in ss-g7-ancient-kingdoms-map and ss-g7-scramble-partition-map — this avoids both factual-boundary-accuracy risk and giving the answer away via a printed country name.

images.prompt: Create a clean, simplified educational geology cross-section diagram titled 'FORMATION OF A RIFT VALLEY AND BLOCK MOUNTAINS' (spell the word 'OF' correctly as the plain word 'OF' — do NOT substitute an ampersand or any other symbol for it) at the top in bold sans-serif capitals. Style: flat educational-textbook illustration (not photorealistic), simple clean line-art with light flat earth-tone colour fills (warm browns and tans for rock layers, soft green for a thin topsoil/vegetation line on top), on a fully solid plain WHITE background, no sky or scenery beyond the rock cross-section itself. Wide landscape composition: draw a wide horizontal cross-section block of the earth's crust showing THREE adjacent vertical blocks of rock separated by two clearly-drawn diagonal fault lines (cracks) — the LEFT block standing tall (a raised block mountain), the MIDDLE block sunk noticeably lower than the two either side (a rift valley floor, with a thin blue line or two representing a lake on its floor), and the RIGHT block also standing tall (a second raised block mountain, roughly matching the left one in height). Draw a pair of bold opposing horizontal arrows well ABOVE the whole diagram, pointing away from each other, in the empty white space at the top-centre of the image, clear of both fault lines, to represent the pulling-apart tension force. Draw a steep near-vertical cliff face on the RIGHT fault line specifically (make the right crack visibly steeper/sharper/more jagged than the left crack, which should look like an ordinary straight diagonal line) — this steeper right-hand crack is the escarpment; the plainer left-hand crack is just the fault line. There are EXACTLY 5 features to mark, and each MUST be placed in its own separate named zone so none of the 5 circles are near each other: (A) — place in the FAR-LEFT margin, leader line touching only the plain LEFT fault-line crack, low down near where it meets the valley floor; (B) — place ABOVE the diagram in the top-CENTRE margin, touching the tension-arrows pair; (C) — place in the BOTTOM-CENTRE margin below the diagram, leader line reaching UP to touch the sunken valley floor / lake area in the middle block; (D) — place in the TOP-RIGHT margin, leader line touching the flat top surface of the RIGHT raised block only; (E) — place in the LOWER-RIGHT margin (below D, clearly separated from it), leader line touching a point precisely ON the steep jagged diagonal crack line itself (the escarpment face, where the middle block drops down) — NOT on the flat outer wall of the right block, NOT at the same point as D; the dot must sit directly on the zigzag crack line. For EACH of these 5, and ONLY these 5, draw one thin dark-grey leader line from a small solid black circle in that feature's assigned margin zone, containing a bold white capital letter, with the line's other end touching a single small dot on the exact feature. CRITICAL COMPLIANCE, checked strictly, this exact prompt has failed vision review twice already: each letter A-E appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole image as one circle with one leader line — do NOT print any letter anywhere except inside its one circle (no bare duplicate letters floating near a crack); do NOT let any two circles' leader lines touch the same point or feature; do NOT print any word from this forbidden list in any spelling: 'fault', 'tension', 'rift valley', 'block mountain', 'escarpment'. Only the title and the 5 lettered circles may contain text. No watermarks, no extra text, no extra graphics.
